text:
Hi team — hitting a reproducible OOM on a one-time Postgres → Iceberg full refresh, and would like guidance on the right way to configure this (and whether some of it needs a product change).

Setup
• OLake v0.12.0 (olakego/source-postgres:v0.12.0), OLake UI + workers on GKE via olake-helm
• Source: PostgreSQL 18.4, standalone (no CDC), max_threads: 2, retry_count: 5
• Destination: Iceberg, REST catalog (Lakekeeper 0.10.4), S3-compatible storage (Wasabi, remote signing). Legacy writer (arrow_writes not set)
• Sync pod node: dedicated pool, 8 vCPU / 32 GB (28.9 GB allocatable), otherwise idle

The table — this is the unusual part
rows            : 78,523,153
heap            : 16 GB
TOAST           : 4,488 GB   <-- two large jsonb columns
indexes         : 23 GB
total           : 4,527 GB
avg JSON/row    : ~131 KB  (jsonb col A ~39.5 KB + col B ~79.7 KB)
total on wire   : ~10.3 TB

What happens
Sync pod is OOMKilled (exit 137) ~96 s in, every run. Relevant log lines:
Starting backfill for stream[<table>] with 9 chunks
Iceberg[50051] ... Successfully wrote 8361 events for thread: <table>_min['(1048576,0)']-max['(1310720,0)'] across 0 files
worker.log: pod sync-... failed (exit code: 137, reason: OOMKilled)
state.json: {}

What we think is going on (from reading v0.12.0 — please correct us)
1. Postgres backfill chunks by ctid page ranges sized at constants.EffectiveParquetSize (2 GB) ÷ block size → 262,144 blocks per chunk. That's derived from relpages, i.e. heap only, so TOAST is invisible to it: 16 GB heap → 9 chunks, but each chunk really carries ~8.7M rows / ~500 GB of JSON.
2. destination/writers.go flushes a writer thread at 10k records or MaxDestinationBatchBytes (1 GB). At 131 KB/row the byte cap fires first — 8,361 × 131 KB ≈ 1.09 GB, which matches the "8361 events" line — and the legacy writer hands that whole batch to the Java writer to materialize in heap.
3. java_client.go launches the writer with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0, but the sync pod has no memory limit (pod.go hardcodes requests: 256Mi/100m, no limits), so the JVM computes its ceiling from the node's 32 GB → ~24 GB max heap. It grows into that instead of GCing, and the node OOMs.

Questions
1. Is there a recommended configuration for TOAST-heavy tables like this? Should chunk sizing consider pg_total_relation_size / avg row width rather than relpages, or is chunk_column on an int PK the intended answer here? Any concern with ~8,600 chunks (10k-id splits) at max_threads: 2?
2. Full-refresh streams get ClearState + destination drop on every run, so a failure restarts from zero (and re-drops the table). For a one-time dump that's a ~2-day single-shot with no checkpoint. Is incremental mode with an int cursor + append_mode the recommended way to get a resumable backfill, or is there a better pattern?
3. Sizing guidance: for ~10 TB / 131 KB rows, what pod memory + max_threads would you recommend? We measured ~27 MB/s per connection from the pod to the source, so at 2 threads this is ~50+ hours of reading — anything else we should tune for a run that long?

I have attached full logs. Thanks!
